821-about-the-bieler-school-of-environme: A trans-disciplinary school run by Arts, Science, and Agricultural and Environmental Sciences. Environmental problems sit where nature meets human systems, so programs start broad across social and natural sciences before specializing.
Its mission: environmental literacy for undergraduates, graduate leaders and researchers, and cross-disciplinary research and outreach.
Offers B.Sc.(Ag.Env.Sc.) and B.Sc. Majors, a B.A. & Sc. Interfaculty Program, a B.A. Faculty Program, a Minor and a Diploma. Most have Honours or Joint Honours, on either or both campuses.
822-admissions-and-program-regulations: Covers admission and the rules for Environment programs.
822-admission: Taken within a B.A., B.A. & Sc., or B.Sc. (Downtown) or B.Sc.(Ag.Env.Sc.) (Macdonald); your admitting faculty's rules apply. Bachelor's graduates may enter the Diploma through any of the three faculties.
822-courses-outside-the-student-s-facult: Follows your admitting faculty's rules, which differ. Science students: some courses are restricted, so check the approved list or ask SOUSA.
822-degree-requirements: Meet your faculty's degree requirements as well as the program's: Arts (p. 151), B.A. & Sc. (p. 430), Agricultural and Environmental Sciences (p. 88), Science (p. 1106), Diploma (p. 870), Honours (p. 865), Joint Honours (pp. 152, 868).
822-examination-regulations: The faculty offering a course sets its evaluation and deferred or supplemental exam rules. All ENVR courses are offered through Science, wherever they are taught.
822-available-programs: Minor or Minor Concentration for all undergraduates; Faculty Program for B.A.; Interfaculty Program for B.A. & Sc.; Major for B.Sc.(Ag.Env.Sc.) and B.Sc.; Honours for all of these; Joint Honours for B.A.; Diploma for those with a Bachelor's, through three faculties.
A core plus a specialization, preparing you for graduate study, industry, government and education.
823-suggested-courses-for-foundation-pro: Foundation Program and U0 students: see your faculty's site for course advice.
823-minor-in-environment: Complements a program outside the School. Arts, Law and Management students do the Minor Concentration; Agricultural and Environmental Sciences, Engineering and Science students do the Minor.
829-b-a-faculty-program-in-environment: Three concentrations: Ecological Determinants of Health in Society, Economics and the Earth's Environment, and Environment and Development. All take 21 credits of core ENVR courses.
829-program-description: Human health and the environment, from both sides: biology and ecology, plus how demographics, economics, ethics, Indigenous knowledge and social change shape interventions. Focus on nutrition and infection.
829-program-prerequisites-or-corequisite: Finish these by the end of U1. S/U is allowed.
829-suggested-first-year-u1-courses: See the Bieler School's Student Handbook.
829-program-requirements: At most 30 credits at the 200 level, and at least 12 at 400+, counting core and required courses but not prerequisites. Courses run on both campuses, so check locations.
830-statistics: One statistics course or equivalent. Overlap rules apply: see Arts' Course Overlap.
831-techniques-and-management: ENVB 529 or GEOG 201, or an advanced quantitative methods course with Adviser approval.
832-program-description: Economics and Earth science together: geology helps limit the harm from extraction and waste, but economics often decides how the environment gets used. You learn minerals, rocks, soils, waters and how they interact, and the economics of resource policy, waste and warming, then combine them on current issues in the final year.
832-core-required-courses-18-credits: Register in ENVR Section 001 Downtown and Section 051 at Macdonald.
833-statistics-3-credits: One statistics course or equivalent. Overlap rules apply: see Arts' Course Overlap.
833-area-1-development-environmental-man: Only one each of ENVB 529 or GEOG 201, BIOL 451 or NRSC 451, ANTH 451 or GEOG 451.
834-area-2-environmental-resources: Only one each of BREE 217 or GEOG 322, BIOL 308 or ENVB 305.
834-program-description: How environment and development interact: nature, economic growth theory, cultural ideas of nature, global economic and environmental bodies, sustainability, and the climate crisis.
834-basic-science: 3 credits or equivalent, such as CEGEP Biology OOUK, Chemistry OOUL or Physics OOUR.
834-required-courses-30-credits: Register in ENVR Section 001 Downtown and Section 051 at Macdonald.
835-natural-sciences: Only one each of BIOL 308 or ENVB 305, BIOL 465 or WILD 421, ENVB 210 or GEOG 305, BREE 217 or GEOG 322.
837-bachelor-of-arts-and-science-b-a-sc-: Liberal arts plus natural science, with flexibility to build skills for many environmental problems. 21 core ENVR credits, then areas you choose.
840-major-in-environment-b-sc-ag-env-sc-: Concentrations: Biodiversity and Conservation; Ecological Determinants of Health (Population and Cellular streams); Environmetrics; Food Production and Environment; Land Surface Processes and Environmental Change; Renewable Resource Management; Water Environments and Ecosystems (Biological and Physical streams). All take 21 core ENVR credits.
B.Sc. (Science) students may also choose Earth Sciences and Economics, or Atmospheric Environment and Air Quality.
840-program-description: 63 credits with the core, for B.Sc.(Ag.Env.Sc.) and B.Sc. Environment Majors only. Connects biodiversity, where evolution, ecology and genetics meet, with conservation biology, which applies those ideas in social and economic settings to prevent extinctions and keep communities diverse.
840-program-requirements: At most 30 credits at the 200 level, and at least 12 at 400+, counting core and required courses. Courses run on both campuses, so check locations.
840-required-courses-18-credits: Register in ENVR Section 001 Downtown and Section 051 at Macdonald.
